item.title: Fostering sustainable university-community partnerships
item.description: This study reflects upon four-year socially engaged scholarship efforts that led to establishing an in-house facility at a public mental healthcare centre in Gauteng, South Africa. item.title: Documentation and integration of indigenous knowledge in public libraries for inclusive information services in Ghana
item.description: The dominance of colonial supremacy and foreign knowledge has become persistent in many African public libraries and knowledge acquisition, including Ghana. Hence, some of the local communities' information needs may be denied due to public libraries' inability to supply indigenous knowledge (IK). This study, therefore, sought to assess the documentation and integration of IK in public libraries in Ghana. item.title: Preservation management framework in library and archival institutions
item.description: On a daily basis, organisations, both government and non-government, produce a lot of goods, provide services and create records as evidence of their business transactions. It is therefore critical to acquire, preserve, and disseminate the various artefacts, goods, and information resources as evidence of the world’s social, intellectual, artistic, and spiritual achievements. item.title: Preserving and indigenising chieftainship cultural heritage in Lesotho
item.description: This study explored aims and progress of preserving and indigenising chieftainship and the monarch’s cultural heritage, the case of Royal Archives, Museum and Information Centre (RAM) in Lesotho. item.title: Safeguarding Basotho heritage
item.description: This paper investigates how the Lesotho National Library Services (LNLS) safeguards Basotho cultural heritage through the Lesotho Collection and the challenges it faces in sustaining effective digital preservation. item.title: Preserving the past, present and future
item.description: Audio-visual recordings generated by public broadcasters contribute to a nation's collection of cultural heritage materials. Broadcasters have a responsibility to ensure that these recordings are preserved for future use to ensure that a nation's historical and cultural assets are preserved. item.title: Preserving language through digital neologisms
item.description: This paper examines the role of neologisms in preserving linguistic knowledge, focusing on how digital platforms, particularly social media, contribute to the creation, dissemination, and preservation of these terms in the digital age. item.description: Translation, along with interpreting and prostitution, is said to be one of the oldest professions in the world. item.title: A case for black sartorial history
item.description: In this article, we investigate black sartoriality through oral history, archives, museums, and libraries by focusing on Martin Molefe, the South African black fashion designer. item.title: Will artificial intelligence replace human librarians?
item.description: This study explores whether artificial intelligence (AI) will replace human librarians, offering an analysis of the evolving role of librarianship in the AI era. The rapid advancement of AI technologies has transformed various industries, and libraries are no exception. item.title: The impact of load shedding on information organisation education in South Africa
item.description: A well-educated and highly skilled information organisation workforce is essential in the current information environment.
